where: crates/hir/src/semantics/child_by_source.rs (the maps from a syntax pointer to a def), read by crates/hir/src/semantics/view/source_to_def.rs and so by blaze-diagnostics' names check
what: tempo's cold build had one compile error in 7,909 units: zone-node, crates/zones/node/src/role.rs:924, `error[E0425]: cannot find type `_0` in this scope ... this error originates in the macro `$crate::select_priv_declare_output_enum``, and the same for `_1`, on a `tokio::select!` rustc accepts. The brief's four candidate causes were all about hygiene and the proc macro; the code read says neither is involved: role.rs:1015 is the same `select!` text as :924 in the same function, and the first of the two is the one refused.
cost: one unit of tempo not built (zone-node and what depends on it); a lane whose brief pointed at hygiene and proc macros
cause: `impl ChildBySource for DefWithBodyId` put every block of the body into the map of whatever file was asked, keyed by `block.ast_id(db).to_ptr(db)`: an `AstPtr`, kind and text range with no file. Two macro calls of the same tokens expand to the same text, so their blocks have equal keys and the later one replaced the earlier. `module_to_def` of the first expansion's `mod __tokio_select_util` then got the second expansion's block and module; that module has no enum in the first expansion's file, `find_container` walked past the enum to the module, and the module's resolver has no generic parameters. Shown by the red run on 8e9c163248 plus the two tests (main agent, Mac): hir's test failed at `each expansion's mod util is the module of its own block` with both sides `Module Id(17412) in BlockId(44033)`, and blaze-diagnostics' gave `E0425: cannot find type `_0` in this scope` and the same for `_1`.
whys: why wrong: `_0` in `enum Out<_0, _1> { _0(_0), .. }` was looked up in a module, not in the enum that declares it
why possible: the enum's syntax mapped to no def, and `find_container` goes on to the next ancestor when one maps to nothing, so a failed lookup became a wider scope instead of an error
why no def: the `mod` around it mapped to the module of the other expansion's block, which has no item in this file
why the other block: the map from a block's pointer to its `BlockId` is asked for one file and was filled with the blocks of every file of the body; the key has no file

why not caught: every other insert in child_by_source.rs filters by file by hand (`.filter(|(id, _)| id.file_id == file_id)`), two did not (the body's blocks, a variant's fields and expansions), and nothing in the type says a pointer belongs to a file
property: a map keyed by a pointer that is only unique within one file can be filled from any file, and each insert site must remember to filter
class: a key that does not cover an input (rule 21) in source-to-def: an `AstPtr` (kind, range) used as a key where nodes of more than one file meet. Every instance: two expansions of the same text in one body or one item (two equal `tokio::select!` in a function; any macro whose expansion is a block declaring a `mod`, called twice with the same tokens), or a node of the source file and a node of an expansion that share kind and range. Its neighbour, a fallback (rule 3): `find_container` took `this item maps to no def` for `try the item further out`, so a wrong map showed up as a missing name far from the cause
prevention: written, not compiled and not run by the lane (write-only): the main agent's runs are the proof. (1) `hir_def::dyn_map::DynMap` is of one file (`DynMap::of(file)`, `file()`); its only insert takes the pointer with its file (`insert(key, InFile<AstPtr>, value)`) and keeps pointers of the map's file; `IndexMut` and `KeyMap::insert` are gone, so no site can insert a bare pointer. `child_by_source_to` reads the file from the map (the parallel `file_id` parameter is gone). This also covers the two other unfiltered sites, a variant's fields and its expansions. (2) `find_container` (hir/src/semantics/view/source_to_def.rs) walks past an item that holds defs and maps to none only for a typed reason, `Unmapped::RemovedByCfg` (a `cfg` removes it or something around it) or `Unmapped::AttributeMacroInput` (it or something around it is an attribute macro's input, whose defs come from the expansion); any other panics naming the item, its file and range and the node asked about. Tests: hir `each_of_two_identical_expansions_in_a_body_maps_its_block_module_and_enum_to_its_own_defs`, its control `planted_blocks_of_any_file_make_the_two_expansions_modules_one` (the planted old behaviour, `BLOCKS_OF_ANY_FILE`), `an_enum_that_maps_to_no_def_is_named_not_walked_past` (should_panic under the plant), `a_node_in_an_item_a_cfg_removes_has_the_scope_around_it`; hir-def `a_pointer_of_another_file_is_not_of_the_map`; blaze-diagnostics `an_enum_in_a_module_of_each_of_two_identical_expansions_in_one_body_sees_its_generics`. Not done, each a way the same class can still happen: `module_to_def` finds an inline module by name in its parent, so of two `mod imp` under opposite cfgs the removed one maps to the kept one; an item in a block of a signature (an array length in a type: static_assertions' `const_assert!`) is in no map `find_container` reads and would now be refused by name if a caller asks about a node in it (none found in the names check, whose scopes are the blocks of bodies; other callers not checked); two different values under one pointer of one file are still last-wins; `AttributeMacroInput` has no test (no proc-macro fixture written).
workaround: none in blaze; not tried: making the two calls differ in length, which by the cause above would give their blocks different ranges
